text:
maya: hi — uploaded an nsys capture for the 64-token regression on ded-rt1. noticed a big jump in tail latency. initial skim shows attention kernels dominating when KV cache hit rate is high. link: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2198765432

perf-bot: automated summary: top kernels by GPU time from capture 2198765432:

```
Kernel                              Time%   Calls   Avg ms   SM Util%
attention_fwd_cuda                  53.2    912     0.18     94
kv_prefetch_async                   11.9    124     0.85     76
softmax_stable                      8.4     912     0.03     65
layernorm_x                          6.1    912     0.02     32
memcpy_h2d                          4.6     48      1.4      12
```

Notes: high attention_fwd SM util (94%) and noticeable kv_prefetch time (12% of GPU time).

arjun: thanks — that SM util is the clue. suspecting contention: our KV prefetch launches persistent kernels that overlap with attention. when cache hit rate is high, prefetch work increases and steals SM slots causing attention to stall/backpressure.

sam: was there any change to batching heuristics lately? we moved to pack up to 8 small requests into a single batch last week (pack_size=8), that could raise concurrent active warps.

maya: yes we flipped pack_size to 8 in the last deploy. good call. could that increase KV prefetch concurrency?

arjun: yep. KV prefetch is per-request right now (we prefetch keys for each request async). with packing, prefetch requests multiply and become concurrent. two quick checks:
1) reproduce with pack_size=1 (no packing) to see if attention_sm_util drops.
2) run nsys with nvtx ranges around kv_prefetch to inspect overlap.

lucy: also check that recent block-size experiment (attention kernel: threads_per_block from 128 -> 256) didn't change occupancy characteristics. increasing threads per block can lower achieved occupancy depending on shared memory. small change but could amplify when SMs are saturated.

arjun: small perfetto timeline snippet from the capture (simplified):
```
[0ms] ├─ batch_inflight (NVTX)
[0-2ms] │  ├─ kv_prefetch (async)  --- runs on stream 2
[1-3ms] │  └─ attention_fwd (main) --- runs on stream 0 (overlap @1-2ms)
[3-6ms] └─ decode loop ...
```
Overlap window exactly where attention spikes.

sam: ok that's actionable. if KV prefetch is async on a separate stream, throttling number of concurrent prefetch kernels or serializing them might reduce SM contention. tradeoff = slightly higher fetch latency but lower tail for attention.

maya: can we try two quick toggles: a) pack_size back to 1 b) kv_prefetch max-concurrency=2 ? I'll run (a) on ded-rt1 smoke cluster now.

arjun: i'll run an isolated nsys capture with nvtx ranges and `--capture-range=nvtx` and grep the kernel order. command i used locally: 
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/out --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --sample=none 
  --force-overwrite --wait=100 --sleep=0 --target-processes=all -- 
  ./run_inference --config=perf/64tok.json --pack_size=1
```
then extract top kernels with: `nsys stats /tmp/out.qdrep --report=cupti_driver`

lucy: i'll prepare a small kernel-weighting patch in runtime scheduler to prefer attention kernels on hot SMs (soft-preempt kv_prefetch). basically if attention_fwd util > 85% for >100ms window, reduce prefetch concurrency. put draft in a PR.

perf-bot: suggestion: quick mitigation -> set pack_size=1 for high-QPS ded pools; set kv_prefetch.max_concurrency=2; add nvtx markers for prefetch to make future captures easier.

maya: done — started pack_size=1 run, linking new capture: https://artifacts.internal/nsys/2198765456

sam: i'll monitor latency p50/p95 during runs. if p95 drops, we know packing was the main factor.

arjun: action items:
- arjun: run isolated nsys captures with pack_size={1,4,8} and attach perfetto timelines (target: today)
- maya: run production-ish smoke with kv_prefetch.max_concurrency=2 (on ded-rt1) and collect traces (target: today)
- lucy: open PR for soft-preempt prefetch heuristic, include guardrails and metrics (target: EOD)

maya: thanks, everyone. ping me when you have captures. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: recorded action items in #perf-playbook (incident ref 2198765432).
